text: Day-blindness: Ger. Tagblindheit ; Fr. nyctalopie ; Ital. cecità diurna , emeralopia . A symptom rather than a distinct disorder, characterized by an inability to see clearly in strong light. Nyctalopia is also used. It may be due to hyperaesthesia of the retina, and result in a clearer vision by dim light or at night, than in full daylight. In suddenly passing from darkness to bright light a transient form of normal day-blindness may be said to exist. The opposite condition is Night-blindness. See Fuchs, Textbook of Ophthalmia (trans. 1899), 496. ( J.J. )
